holidays.name: Global Smurfs Day
holidays.description: Fans around the world break out their white hats and paint themselves blue. They binge old cartoons and celebrate the little blue villagers who live in mushroom houses. Expect plenty of Smurfberry-themed snacks and a lot of "smurfing" in everyday sentences.
holidays.origin: The Smurfs were created by Belgian cartoonist Peyo (Pierre Culliford), who first introduced them in a Belgian comic magazine in 1958. Global Smurfs Day is an unofficial fan celebration of the franchise.
holidays.funFact: Peyo reportedly came up with the name on the spot. At a meal he couldn't remember the word for salt shaker and asked for the 'schtroumpf', a nonsense word that became the Smurfs' name.

holidays.name: National Chocolate Pudding Day
holidays.description: A day to dig a spoon into a silky, chocolatey cup of nostalgia. Eat it warm from the stovetop or cold from the fridge, and don't skip the skin if that's your thing. It's a good excuse to eat dessert without guilt.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It is listed among the American dessert-themed days that fall in late June.
holidays.funFact: Pudding is one of the oldest comfort desserts. It began as a savory dish of meat and grains boiled in a cloth bag, and it only became sweet and creamy over the centuries.

holidays.name: National Beautician's Day
holidays.description: This day thanks the stylists, cosmetologists, and hair wizards who fix bad haircuts and boost people's confidence. Book an appointment, leave a big tip, or just tell your stylist they're a genius.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is celebrated in the United States every year on June 26.
holidays.funFact: Many stylists say they hear more secrets than a bartender or a therapist, which has made the salon chair one of the most trusted seats in town.
